selection.reason: Impact scored and summarised by Gemini. (rated before the current eligibility rules; kept)

summary: The No Troops in Our Streets Act of 2026 allows Congress to end exceptions to the prohibition on using the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Space Force for law enforcement (posse comitatus), as well as certain National Guard activations, by passing a joint resolution of disapproval. It also appropriates $900 million in fiscal year 2026 for various state and local law enforcement assistance programs, community violence initiatives, emergency law enforcement assistance, and hiring career law enforcement officers, while explicitly prohibiting these funds from being used to assign federal law enforcement personnel to states and localities.

affected_groups.effect: Subject to potential congressional termination of exceptions that allow their deployment for domestic law enforcement or other posse comitatus exceptions.
affected_groups.group: U.S. Armed Forces (Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Space Force)

affected_groups.effect: Eligible to receive a total of $900 million in federal funding for grant programs, violence prevention, emergency assistance, and hiring career officers, but barred from using these funds to assign federal law enforcement personnel to their jurisdictions.
affected_groups.group: State and Local Law Enforcement Agencies

affected_groups.effect: Gains expedited procedures and specific authority to pass joint resolutions of disapproval to halt military deployments and certain National Guard activations.

key_provisions: Establishes a formal legislative mechanism (a joint resolution of disapproval) for Congress to terminate exceptions to the prohibition on using military forces as posse comitatus.
Provides specific legislative procedures and expedited committee discharge rules for considering joint resolutions of disapproval in both the Senate and the House of Representatives.
Permits Congress to terminate National Guard activations under section 12406 of title 10, United States Code, using the same joint resolution of disapproval process.
Appropriates $600 million for the Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant program for fiscal year 2026.
Appropriates $150 million for a community violence intervention and prevention initiative and $50 million for emergency law enforcement assistance for fiscal year 2026.
Appropriates $100 million for grants to hire and rehire additional career law enforcement officers for fiscal year 2026.
Prohibits any of the newly appropriated grant funds from being used to fund the assignment of federal law enforcement personnel to states and localities.
missing_information: The text does not specify the exact pre-existing exceptions to the posse comitatus prohibition that may be targeted beyond establishing the termination mechanism.

The text does not detail the specific statutory formulas or allocation criteria for how the $600 million Byrne JAG funds are distributed to individual jurisdictions outside of noting that certain existing code sections do not apply.
summary_detail.plain_summary: The No Troops in Our Streets Act of 2026 allows Congress to end exceptions to the prohibition on using the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force, and Space Force for law enforcement (posse comitatus), as well as certain National Guard activations, by passing a joint resolution of disapproval. It also appropriates $900 million in fiscal year 2026 for various state and local law enforcement assistance programs, community violence initiatives, emergency law enforcement assistance, and hiring career law enforcement officers, while explicitly prohibiting these funds from being used to assign federal law enforcement personnel to states and localities.
summary_detail.significance: The bill alters the balance of power between the executive and legislative branches regarding the domestic use of the military and National Guard by creating an expedited legislative veto via joint resolutions. Additionally, it injects $900 million into federal state and local law enforcement assistance grants for fiscal year 2026.
